verdict.rationale: Unity documents public scripting APIs for finer control of the product, and its documented first-party CLI drives the Editor directly via `unity <command>`/`unity eval`, with structured JSON/TSV output and documented exit codes. Together these give an agent a documented programmatic surface. Missing for 10: no HTTP/REST or OpenAPI spec (all OpenAPI probe paths returned 404), the standalone CLI is still experimental, the manual is not machine-readable (no llms.txt or .md mirrors on docs.unity3d.com), and there is no hands-on corroboration of agent-driven API use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: Interacting directly with the public Unity APIs allows for finer control and a greater degree of customization.
`unity <command>`/`unity eval` drive the Editor directly without MCP
You can launch the Unity Editor and Player with additional command line arguments to control startup behavior, configure settings, or automate workflows.
